mainTopic: Whether a derived law can teach further in קדשים, and the sources for pouring leftover blood on the base of the outer altar
overview: This amud begins in the middle of a ברייתא the גמרא brought as a proof. The ברייתא says that slaughter purifies a kosher bird that is a טריפה, and that מליקה should do the same, while רבי יוסי limits this using the rule of דיו. The גמרא rejects the proof, because that chain of learning starts from the slaughter of חולין, and the question is only about קדשים. Next the גמרא asks whether a law learned through a בנין אב can go on to teach another law. It tries to answer from a ברייתא that learns several disqualified offerings from one another, but it then shows that the real source is the פסוק ״זאת תורת העולה״, so the comparisons are only supports. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that leftover blood is poured on the western base of the outer altar, the side a כהן meets first coming out. A ברייתא reads the phrase ״אל יסוד מזבח העולה״ three times: not the inner altar's base, the inner altar has no base at all, and blood placed on the outer altar also has its leftovers poured on the base. The גמרא examines the first of these readings and begins examining the third, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Pinching should purify a טריפה bird just like slaughter does
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its comparison. Slaughter purifies a טריפה bird from its impurity because slaughter makes the bird permitted to eat. So מליקה, which also makes a bird offering permitted to eat, should purify it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Slaughter, which makes the bird permitted to eat,] purifies its טריפה from its impurity. So too מליקה, which makes it permitted to eat, should purify its טריפה from its impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: We join in the middle of a ברייתא that the גמרא is using as a proof. The ברייתא compares מליקה to שחיטה and says both should remove the impurity of a טריפה bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law that slaughter purifies a טריפה bird was itself learned through a derivation. Now that learned law is used as a model (a 'מה... אף...' comparison) to teach a new law about מליקה. The גמרא wants to show that a law which was learned can go on to teach another law.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even if slaughtered properly
Pinching the back of the neck of a bird offering; this is how a bird קרבן is killed instead of שחיטה
It makes it permitted to be eaten
Ritual impurity; here, the impurity of a dead kosher bird (נבלת עוף טהור)
'Just as... so too...', the wording of a comparison that builds a model

phrases.english: purifies its tereifa from its impurity;
phrases.notes: The subject here is שחיטה, the slaughter, which makes the bird permitted to eat.

phrases.english: so too pinching, which permits it to be eaten,
should purify its tereifa from its impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that the גמרא brought earlier as a proof, before this section begins.
steps.raayaObject: That in קדשים, a law which was itself derived can go on to teach another law through a further derivation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about נבלת עוף טהור: the purifying power of slaughter is carried over to מליקה through a 'מה... אף...' comparison.

steps.title: רבי יוסי limits it: only slaughter purifies, not pinching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the bird can be no better than the source it was learned from, a kosher animal. A kosher animal is purified only by שחיטה, so the bird is also purified only by שחיטה and not by מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: It is enough for it to be like the carcass of a kosher animal, which only its slaughter purifies, and not its pinching.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי disagrees with the extension to מליקה. He says the bird's law cannot go further than the animal law it came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the rule of דיו: something learned through a קל וחומר cannot be stronger than its source. An animal is never killed by מליקה, so the bird's law, which came from the animal, should also stop at שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is enough': a law learned through a קל וחומר cannot be stronger than its source
The carcass of a kosher animal that died without proper slaughter
Kosher slaughter with a knife at the throat

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying that slaughter fails to purify a טריפה bird. He agrees that it does. He only refuses to extend that purifying power to מליקה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
It is enough for it to be like the carcass of a kosher animal,
phrases.notes: Literally 'it is enough for it.' He means the bird's law can be no better than the animal law it was learned from.

phrases.english: which its slaughter purifies, but not its pinching.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: דַּיָּהּ כְּנִבְלַת בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion inside the same ברייתא that limits the comparison made in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using the rule of דיו, a טריפה bird is purified only through שחיטה, not through מליקה.

steps.title: No proof, because the source comes from חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The law that slaughter purifies a bird comes from the slaughter of non-sacred (חולין) animals. Our question is only about קדשים, so this ברייתא proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not so. Leave that case there, because those laws come from the slaughter of חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the ברייתא. It says the case cannot settle our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that in חולין a law which was learned can teach another law. The open question was only about קדשים. Since the chain in this ברייתא starts from חולין slaughter, it does not show anything about the rules of קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is not so': the proof is rejected
'Let it stay there': that case stands on its own and teaches nothing here
Non-sacred, ordinary animals, as opposed to קדשים

steps.whatToRemember: A proof only counts if its source is also in the world of קדשים. A derivation chain that starts from חולין cannot answer a question about the rules of קדשים.

phrases.english: And it is not so;
let it remain there,
phrases.notes: In other words, that case is a different story, so we can't learn from it.

phrases.english: they come from the slaughter of non-sacred animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought from the ברייתא in steps 1-2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The ברייתא's own laws are not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The derivation chain starts from the slaughter of חולין, while the question is only about how derivations work in קדשים.

steps.title: New question: can a law learned through בנין אב teach further?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new inquiry. If a law in קדשים was learned through a בנין אב, can it then teach another law through a היקש, a גזירה שוה, a קל וחומר, or another בנין אב?
steps.simpleTranslation: A matter learned through a בנין אב: may it teach through a היקש, a גזירה שוה, a קל וחומר, or a בנין אב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question in the same series. This line sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier questions asked about laws learned through other methods. Now the starting method is a בנין אב, and the גמרא asks about each of the four possible ways it could teach next. Like the earlier questions, this is about the rules of קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Building a general rule from one or more source cases
Comparing two subjects because the תורה placed them together
Comparing two passages that use the same word
Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter case
A law that was learned from somewhere else

phrases.english: A matter learned through a paradigm,
what is the law about whether it may teach through a juxtaposition

phrases.aramaic: וּבִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה וּבְקַל וָחוֹמֶר וּבְבִנְיַן אָב?
phrases.english: or through a verbal analogy, or through an a fortiori inference, or through a paradigm?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּבִנְיַן אָב, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous inquiry ends without a proof, the גמרא moves on to the next inquiry in the series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, in קדשים, a law learned through a בנין אב can go on to teach through each of the four methods of derivation.

steps.title: Resolve at least one question: blood left overnight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets out to resolve at least one of its questions. It quotes a ברייתא where blood left overnight is learned from אימורין, which are themselves learned from meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us at least resolve one of the questions. Why did they say that blood left overnight is fit? Because אימורין left overnight are fit. And why are אימורין left overnight fit? Because meat left overnight is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof. It quotes a ברייתא that it will soon use to answer at least one of the questions from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds a chain. The law about blood is learned from the אימורין, and the law about the אימורין was itself learned from the meat. So a law that was learned is used to teach another law, and that is exactly the kind of case Step 4 asked about.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve, answer (a question)
Left overnight, past the time it should have been offered
The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח (fats and certain organs)
Here: valid enough that it does not have to be taken down from the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Here כָּשֵׁר does not mean the offering was done properly from the start. It means that once it is already on the מזבח, it is not taken down.
steps.whyThisMatters: This chain of 'learned from something that was itself learned' is the raw material the גמרא needs to answer whether a learned law can teach again.

phrases.english: Resolve at least one [of these questions]:
phrases.notes: He means one of the questions from Step 4: can a law learned through a בנין אב go on to teach another law?

phrases.english: For what reason did they say:
with blood left overnight, it is fit?
phrases.notes: If the blood was left overnight and then put on the מזבח, it is not removed.

phrases.english: Because with sacrificial portions left overnight, it is fit.
And with sacrificial portions left overnight, it is fit
because with meat left overnight, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the inquiry of Step 4 by quoting a ברייתא that contains a chain of derivations.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a law learned through a בנין אב in קדשים can itself teach another law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: blood left overnight is learned from אימורין left overnight, which are learned from meat left overnight.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: offerings that went out, became impure, or became פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a short reason for each of three more cases. An offering that went out is fit because of a private במה. An impure one is fit because of communal offerings. A פיגול is fit because its blood still brings acceptance.
steps.simpleTranslation: An offering that went out of its area is fit, since going out is allowed at a private במה. An impure offering is fit, since impurity was allowed for communal offerings. One that became פיגול is fit, since its blood still brings acceptance, which is how it becomes פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and lists three more disqualified offerings that are not removed from the מזבח, each with its reason. This finishes quoting the source before the גמרא draws its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case is matched to a situation where the same problem is allowed. Going out is allowed at a private במה, and impurity is allowed in communal offerings. For פיגול, the reason is that the offering still brings acceptance, which shows it still counts as an offering.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering that went out of its allowed area
A private altar, used in times when they were allowed, where there is no set area to leave
Communal offerings, which may be brought even when impure if needed
An offering ruined by planning to eat or offer it after its proper time
Brings acceptance (the offering is accepted)

phrases.english: One that went out:
phrases.notes: An offering that left its proper area, such as the Temple courtyard.

phrases.english: since going out is fit at a private altar.
Impure:
since it was permitted in communal service.
Beyond its time:
since it brings acceptance to make it פיגול.
phrases.notes: An offering only becomes פיגול if everything else was done right, so it still counts as an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא begun in Step 5, adding three more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offering that went out, became impure, or became פיגול is not removed from the מזבח once it went up. Each has its own reason: a private במה, communal offerings, and acceptance despite פיגול.

steps.title: Two more cases in the ברייתא's list
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a reason for two more disqualified offerings that stay on the altar: חוץ למקומו and one whose blood was handled by פסולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: An offering slaughtered with the intent to eat it outside its proper place stays on the altar, because the תורה links it to the case of intent to eat it outside its proper time. An offering whose blood was received and sprinkled by disqualified people also stays, because we see that such people can be fit for communal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the list from the last step. It gives a short source for two more kinds of disqualified offerings that, once on the altar, are not taken down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוץ למקומו is learned from חוץ לזמנו through a הקש, meaning the Torah places the two side by side. The case of פסולין is learned from the fact that impure כהנים may bring communal offerings when everyone is impure. So these people are not totally unfit for service.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent to eat or burn the offering outside its proper place
Intent to eat or burn the offering after its proper time
It was compared or linked by the Torah (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
People who are disqualified from doing the Temple service
Communal service, the offerings brought for the whole nation

phrases.english: An offering disqualified by intent outside its place:
since it is linked to intent outside its time.
Offerings whose blood disqualified people received and sprinkled:
learned from those disqualified people
phrases.notes: He means impure כהנים, who are normally disqualified.

phrases.english: who are fit for communal service.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ הוֹאִיל וְהוּקַּשׁ לְחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of reasons begun in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוץ למקומו is fit through a הקש to חוץ לזמנו. An offering handled by פסולין is fit because פסולין can serve in עבודת ציבור.

steps.title: Can you learn the unfit from the fit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's method: it learns laws about disqualified things from things that are still fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how can we learn the law of something that is disqualified from something that is still in its fit state?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's derivations. They compare disqualified offerings to cases where the offering is perfectly valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For example, אימורין that were left overnight are disqualified. Yet the ברייתא learned them from a שלמים, which may be eaten for two days and a night and is still fit at that point. A comparison only works when both cases are alike, so learning a פסול case from a כשר case looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive or learn one law from another
Fitness, the valid state of something
Something that is not in its fit state, meaning disqualified

phrases.english: But can one derive a matter that is not fit
from a matter that is fit?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בְּהֶכְשֵׁירוֹ מִדָּבָר שֶׁבְּהֶכְשֵׁירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivations the ברייתא gave in steps 5 to 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's derivations of disqualified offerings from valid cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A derivation needs the two cases to be similar. A disqualified item cannot be learned from an item that is still fit.

steps.title: The real source is ״זאת תורת העולה״
steps.stepSummary: The real source is the פסוק ״זאת תורת העולה״, which includes many disqualified offerings. The ברייתא's derivations are only supports.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא really relies on the פסוק 'This is the law of the burnt offering', which included many offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The law truly comes from a פסוק that includes many disqualified offerings, and the ברייתא's comparisons are only extra support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law does not truly rest on the comparisons, so it no longer matters that they compare unfit things to fit things. But this also means the ברייתא is not a real case of a בנין אב teaching another בנין אב. So the proof attempted in step 5 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the law of the burnt offering', the פסוק that is the real source
It included, widening the law to cover more cases
He relies on it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's chain of comparisons is only a support. The real source is the inclusion from ״זאת תורת העולה״, so the ברייתא cannot settle whether a בנין אב can teach through another בנין אב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the ראיה brought in step 5, so the question from step 4 stays open.

phrases.english: The תנא: from 'This is the law of the burnt offering' the Torah included many cases,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:2

phrases.english: and on that he relies.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא מִזֹּאת תּוֹרַת הָעוֹלָה רִיבָּה סָמֵיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the source to a פסוק; the derivations become only supports
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's law depends on its chain of בנין אב derivations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The law comes from the inclusion in ״זאת תורת העולה״, and the derivations are only supports.

steps.title: Why the leftover blood goes on the western base
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about leftover blood and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the leftover blood is poured on the western base of the outer altar. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה about leftover blood and asks why it must go on the western base. This is setting up the next step, where the answer comes from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the inner חטאות, the blood is sprinkled inside the היכל. The leftover blood, the שירי הדם, is then carried out and poured on the base of the outer altar. The גמרא wants to know why it goes on the western side in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood that remains after the required sprinklings
What is the reason / the source?
"Etc.": the rest of the quoted line is left out

phrases.english: "The leftover blood, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: leftover blood from the inner חטאות is poured on the western base of the outer altar.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא about disqualified offerings (steps 5-9) and starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for pouring the leftover blood specifically on the western base.

steps.title: The base you meet first is the western one
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the base of the outer altar "that is at the entrance of the אהל מועד", which means the side you reach first, the west.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "at the base of the altar of the עולה, which is at the entrance of the אהל מועד." That means the base he reaches first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a פסוק. The words "at the entrance of the אהל מועד" point to the part of the altar closest to the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן coming out of the היכל walks east toward the outer altar. The first side of the altar he meets is the western side. So "the base by the entrance" means the western base.

keyTerms.meaning: The base of the altar
He meets it first

phrases.english: The verse says:
"At the base of the altar of the burnt offering,
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:ז

phrases.english: which is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting":
the one he meets first.
phrases.notes: Coming out of the היכל, the first side of the altar he reaches is the west side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא ד:ז, "which is at the entrance of the אהל מועד": the base he reaches first when leaving, which is the western base.

steps.title: Not the base of the inner altar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches from the first appearance of the phrase that the leftover blood goes on the outer altar's base, not the inner altar's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "At the base of the altar of the עולה" means the outer altar, and not the base of the inner altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the same phrase three times. In this first reading, the leftover blood must go to the outer altar, not the inner one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פר כהן משיח's blood is sprinkled on the inner altar. You might think the leftover blood goes at the base of that same altar. The פסוק says "the altar of the עולה", which is the outer altar, so that idea is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer altar, where עולות are brought
The inner (golden) altar inside the היכל

steps.confusionAlert: The same exact words, ״אל יסוד מזבח העולה״, come up three times in this ברייתא. Each one is a different פסוק in ויקרא ד׳, so each one teaches a different point.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"At the base of the altar of the burnt offering":
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:ז, about the bull of the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and not the base of the inner altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that expands on the same פסוק used in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover blood of inner חטאות is poured on the outer altar's base, not the inner altar's.

steps.title: The inner altar has no base at all
steps.stepSummary: The second appearance of the phrase teaches that the inner altar does not have a base.
steps.simpleTranslation: "At the base of the altar of the עולה": the inner altar itself has no base.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the phrase a second time, from the פסוק about the פר העלם דבר של ציבור. This time it teaches that the inner altar has no base at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 only said not to use the inner altar's base. Here the ברייתא goes further: the inner altar was never built with a base in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: It has no base
Itself

phrases.english: "At the base of the altar of the burnt offering":
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:יח

phrases.english: the inner altar itself has no base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second of the ברייתא's three readings; goes a step further than step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner altar has no base.

steps.title: Leftover blood from the outer altar also goes on a base
steps.stepSummary: The third appearance of the phrase teaches that the outer altar's own חטאות also need their leftover blood poured on the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: "At the base of the altar of the עולה": give a base to the altar of the עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the phrase a third time, from the פסוק about the king's חטאת. Here the blood is placed on the outer altar itself, and its leftover blood must also go on the base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two readings dealt with blood from inside the היכל. This one teaches that blood placed on the outer altar also has its leftovers poured on the base. So the rule of pouring on the יסוד covers both kinds of חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: Give a base: pour the leftover blood on the base
The חטאת of a king or leader, brought on the outer altar

steps.whatToRemember: Leftover blood from the inner חטאות goes on the western base of the outer altar, the side you reach first. The inner altar has no base. Leftover blood from blood placed on the outer altar also goes on a base.

phrases.english: "At the base of the altar of the burnt offering":
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:כה

phrases.english: give a base to the altar of the burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last reading in the ברייתא; extends the base rule to blood placed on the outer altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover blood from sprinklings on the outer altar must also be poured on its base.

steps.title: Maybe the verse teaches that an עולה needs a base
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a different reading of the third phrase: maybe it teaches that the blood of an עולה must be placed where the altar has a base.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the verse only means that the altar of the burnt offering should have its blood placed at the base.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another possible meaning for the phrase it just used in step 14. This sets up the next move, which shows why that meaning does not need a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the phrase "אל יסוד מזבח העולה" taught that the outer altar's own חטאות pour their leftover blood on the base. Now the ברייתא asks whether the phrase might instead teach that an עולה's blood must go on a section of the altar that has a base underneath.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it only means: introduces another possible reading
Burnt offering
The altar of the burnt offering, the outer altar

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only teaching
that the altar placement of the burnt offering should be over the base?
phrases.notes: He means the regular sprinkling of an עולה's blood must be done on a part of the altar that has a base under it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִזְבְּחָהּ שֶׁל עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another reading of the phrase step 14 just used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the phrase teach the base rule for leftover blood of outer חטאות, or a base requirement for the blood of an עולה?

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the עולה rule comes from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says no verse is needed for the עולה, because leftover blood, which does not bring atonement, needs a base. So the main blood of an עולה, which does bring atonement, surely needs a base.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: it is a קל וחומר. Leftover blood does not atone, yet it needs the base. The first sprinkling of an עולה does atone, so surely it needs the base.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל shows that the other reading does not need a verse, because simple logic already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר goes from the weaker case to the stronger one. Leftover blood is less important because it does not atone, and it still requires the base. So the atoning blood of an עולה must require it too.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
They bring atonement
The first, main sprinkling of an עולה's blood
Is it not logical?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said: it is an a fortiori argument;
just as the leftover blood, which does not bring atonement,
requires the base;
the first sprinkling of a burnt offering, which does bring atonement,
is it not logical that it requires the base?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by showing that its reading is already known through logic.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The base requirement for an עולה comes from a קל וחומר from leftover blood, so the verse is not needed for it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: an even stronger קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא makes the same argument and adds a second point: leftover blood does not even come for atonement, while the עולה both atones and comes for atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: leftover blood does not atone and does not come for atonement, yet it needs the base. The first sprinkling of an עולה atones and comes for atonement, so surely it needs the base.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his version of the same logical proof, adding one more difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא adds that leftover blood is not even part of the atonement process ("אין באין לכפרה"). That makes the gap between the two cases wider and the קל וחומר stronger. Either way, the עולה rule does not need the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Coming for atonement, being part of the atonement process

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
just as the leftover blood, which does not bring atonement
and does not come for atonement, requires the base;
the first sprinkling of a burnt offering, which brings atonement and comes for atonement,
is it not logical that it requires the base?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, stronger version of רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Same conclusion as step 16, built on two differences instead of one.

steps.title: So the verse teaches base-pouring for the outer altar's own offerings
steps.stepSummary: Since logic already covers the עולה, the verse "אל יסוד מזבח העולה" must teach that the outer altar's own offerings pour their leftover blood on the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say "to the base of the altar of the burnt offering"? To give a base to the altar of the burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes: the other reading is not needed, so the verse goes back to teaching the rule from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse is not written to teach something logic already teaches. Because the עולה rule comes from a קל וחומר, the phrase is free to teach that חטאות placed on the outer altar also need their leftover blood poured on its base.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
Give a base: apply the base-pouring rule

steps.whatToRemember: The third phrase teaches base-pouring for the outer altar's own חטאות. The base requirement for an עולה comes from a קל וחומר, not from a verse.

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse state
"at the base of the altar of the burnt offering"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:25

phrases.english: To give a base to the altar of the burnt offering.
phrases.notes: He means the outer altar's own חטאות also pour their leftover blood on the base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the קל וחומר to set aside the reading from step 15 and confirm step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "אל יסוד מזבח העולה" teaches that the leftover blood of the outer altar's own חטאות goes on the base.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's first derivation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the ברייתא's first teaching: "אל יסוד מזבח" means the outer altar's base, not the inner altar's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: "to the base of the altar", and not the base of the inner altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now examines the ברייתא and quotes its first derivation. This is setup for a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the teaching from step 12 so the גמרא can test whether the phrase is really free to teach this exclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner, golden altar

phrases.english: The Master said:
"at the base of the altar"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:18

phrases.english: and not the base of the inner altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's first derivation to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first phrase excludes the inner altar's base for leftover blood.

steps.title: Isn't the phrase needed for its plain meaning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: this phrase is needed to teach the basic rule that leftover blood goes on the outer altar's base, so how can it also teach an exclusion?
steps.simpleTranslation: But that phrase is needed for the matter itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the derivation it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the phrase is the only source that leftover blood goes on the outer altar's base, it is busy teaching that. Then it cannot also be used to teach the extra point that the inner altar is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for
For itself, its plain basic meaning

phrases.english: But it is needed for the matter itself!
phrases.notes: Meaning the phrase is needed to teach the basic rule: pour the leftover blood on the outer altar's base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of "אל יסוד מזבח" to exclude the inner altar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A phrase needed for its basic meaning cannot also be used for an extra teaching.

steps.title: The basic rule comes from "אשר פתח אהל מועד"
steps.stepSummary: The basic rule comes from the words "אשר פתח אהל מועד", so "מזבח העולה" is free to exclude the inner altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: That comes from "which is at the entrance of the אהל מועד".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a different part of the verse already teaches the basic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אשר פתח אהל מועד" already points to the outer altar, as step 11 explained. So the phrase "מזבח העולה" is not needed for that, and it can teach that the inner altar's base does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived from
The entrance of the אהל מועד, where the outer altar stood

steps.whatToRemember: "אשר פתח אהל מועד" teaches that leftover blood goes on the outer altar's base. "מזבח העולה" then excludes the inner altar.

phrases.english: That is derived from "which is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:18. This is the same phrase used back in step 11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different source in the verse for the basic rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "מזבח העולה" is needed to teach that leftover blood goes on the outer altar's base.
steps.terutzMaskana: "אשר פתח אהל מועד" teaches that, so "מזבח העולה" is free to exclude the inner altar.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the ברייתא about the king's sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now quotes the ברייתא's third reading, "אל יסוד מזבח העולה" from the פסוק about the חטאת of a נשיא, so it can examine that reading the way it examined the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: "At the base of the altar of the burnt offering", the words written about the king's sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: After testing the ברייתא's first reading, the גמרא now quotes its third reading, from the פסוק about the חטאת of a נשיא, in order to examine it. This is only a setup line; the discussion continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third time the phrase appears in the ברייתא. In step 14 the ברייתא used it to teach "תן יסוד": the leftover blood of the outer altar's own חטאות goes on the base, and steps 15-18 confirmed that reading. Now the גמרא returns to that reading to look at it more closely.

keyTerms.meaning: The king or leader, who brings his own special חטאת
A sin offering
The altar of the burnt offering, meaning the outer altar

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same פסוק as the one in steps 19-21. The words are the same, but these come from the פסוק about the king's sin offering (ויקרא 4:25). That is the reading the ברייתא already used in step 14 to teach "תן יסוד".

phrases.english: "At the base of the altar of the burnt offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:25. This is the פסוק about the king's sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After examining the ברייתא's first reading (steps 19-21), the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's third reading (step 14) to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No new ruling. This line re-quotes the ברייתא's third reading ("תן יסוד", step 14) so the גמרא can discuss it.
